James Cherti
The
consult
Emacs package provides asynchronous search commands such as
consult-fd
,
consult-find
,
consult-grep
,
consult-git-grep
, and
consult-ripgrep
. For these commands, Consult does not necessarily start a new search for every change to the minibuffer input. Instead, it uses configurable debounce and throttle delays to control when asynchronous processes start, while a separate refresh delay controls how frequently asynchronous results are pushed to the completion UI.
The first time I tried Consult, I thought to myself: this feels slow compared to Counsel (I had a similar feeling about Emacs settings such as
show-paren-delay
). With Counsel, results updated immediately on every keystroke, while Consult seemed to hesitate for a fraction of a second before updating the list.
As it turns out, this behavior is entirely intentional. The current Consult defaults are conservative by design.
Aggressive asynchronous search
If you prefer lower latency and speed, these variables can be made more aggressive:
(
setq
consult-async-input-debounce
0.05
consult-async-input-throttle
0.1
consult-async-refresh-delay
0.05
)
These values reduce the amount of time Consult waits before starting another asynchronous search and allow the completion UI to refresh much more frequently.
These values do not make the underlying search programs execute faster. External tools like
ripgrep
already use highly optimized, multi-threaded algorithms to scan files across multiple CPU cores. Instead, these variables speed up the feedback loop inside Emacs itself. They reduce the waiting period before Consult spawns the external process, and causing the Emacs UI to pull in new asynchronous data and redraw the screen at a much faster rate.
Variable: consult-async-input-debounce
(
setq
consult-async-input-debounce
0.05
)
This setting forces Consult to wait 0.05 seconds after your last keystroke before launching an asynchronous process. Because this acts as a debounce delay rather than a fixed polling interval, every new input resets the timer. The search only executes once the full quiet period elapses.
This prevents Emacs from spinning up redundant background tasks for every intermediate character you type, which minimizes CPU overhead and keeps the UI responsive.
Variable: consult-async-input-throttle
(
setq
consult-async-input-throttle
0.1
)
The
consult-async-input-throttle
variable acts as a hard rate limit for how often Consult starts asynchronous processes. With this value, a new process starts at most once every 0.1 seconds, regardless of how fast you type.
To break down the difference between the two concepts:
Debouncing is an idle timer. It waits for you to stop typing. If you keep hitting keys, the timer keeps resetting, and the search will not run until you stop typing.
Throttling is a strict speed limit. It enforces a maximum execution rate. Even if you pause just long enough between words to constantly trigger the debounce timer, the throttle ensures the system will not exceed the permitted rate.
Variable: consult-async-refresh-delay
(
setq
consult-async-refresh-delay
0.05
)
The
consult-async-refresh-delay
variable controls how frequently Consult updates the completion UI with results from asynchronous commands. This value makes Consult refresh at intervals as short as 0.05 seconds when new results require an update. It does not cause Emacs to redraw continuously when there is nothing new to display.
A low refresh delay can make search results appear faster, but redisplay itself has a cost. Emacs redisplay is expensive enough that highly frequent updates can increase CPU and garbage-collection activity.
Choosing values
If you prefer asynchronous searches to feel as responsive as possible, these values offer a good balance between low input latency and resource usage. Consult responds quickly to minibuffer changes and updates the completion UI with minimal delay.
These settings are well suited to fast computers plugged into a power source. On a laptop, the aggressive process creation and continuous UI updates will keep the CPU active and drain your battery much faster than the conservative defaults. On slower computers or when searching very large projects, the default values may provide a better balance by avoiding unnecessary searches while input is still changing.
The optimal values depend on typing speed, project size, search-tool performance, power constraints, and the cost of processing and redisplaying asynchronous results in Emacs. Lowering the delays is therefore best viewed as an explicit trade-off: less input latency in exchange for more frequent asynchronous work.

• **对偏见的谨慎担忧**：有人对此并不意外，但希望广告不会实质性影响或扭曲模型输出，体现出对技术可靠性的保留态度。

data.title: Shopify moves back to Native from React Native
data.author: fnthawar2
data.article_summary: Shopify宣布从React Native转向Swift和Kotlin原生开发。公司认为，代码智能体已大幅降低跨平台重复开发、功能对齐、测试和维护成本，使原生开发更具平台能力和工具优势。React Native仍很优秀，但其共享实现的优势已减弱。Shopify将继续支持Skia至2026年底，维护FlashList关键问题，并停止维护Restyle。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI/LLM 编程代理改变了移动应用开发成本与迭代方式，促使部分团队重新评估 React Native、Flutter 与原生 Swift/Kotlin 的取舍，Shopify 回归原生成为讨论焦点。

不同观点：
• 支持回归原生：LLM 已能快速生成并迁移原生代码，原生性能、平台适配和维护体验更好。atonse 称代理在一夜间将约90%的 React Native 应用转换为 Kotlin/Jetpack Compose 和 Swift；也有人认为 RN 做复杂或高性能功能时仍要下沉原生，抽象层价值有限。  
• 支持或仍看好跨平台：React Native/Expo 具备热更新、快速迭代和成熟工具链，尤其适合 AI“氛围编程”应用；pzo 认为 RN 今年已足够成熟，质疑文章未充分解释迁移理由。  
• 条件化、反对绝对化：Waterluvian 认为这是资源与需求约束下的正常工程决策，不应笼统宣称原生或 RN 永远更好；AI 只是让“适用边界”发生移动。也有人建议采用 Swift/Kotlin 原生配合 Rust 共享代码。  
• 行业趋势判断：部分评论预测业界会整体放弃 RN/Flutter、回归原生，但也有人以“React 是否退回原始 JavaScript”反讽这种技术钟摆。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 AI 降低原生开发成本后，跨平台带来的复用优势是否仍足以抵消性能和复杂度代价；评论还关注 Shopify 的渐进迁移与重写、Helix 质量控制机制，以及 RN 生态项目（如 Skia、FlashList）可能受损。

49643982.article_content:
blog
|
Mobile
Native is now the future of mobile at Shopify
Coding agents changed what it costs to build mobile apps twice. Here’s why Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin.
Published on
Sep 10, 2026
We decided to
go all-in
on React Native back in 2020, and that bet has been extremely successful. We saved a ton of time building features just once, enabled developers with no mobile background to contribute to our apps, and freed ourselves from constantly chasing feature parity.
In January 2025, I
wrote
that the future of React Native was bright and that Shopify planned to keep investing in it. That was true based on what we knew then. React Native was working well for us, and it remains an excellent framework. But since then, coding models have gotten dramatically better, and for our apps and our team, building the same feature in Swift and Kotlin no longer carries the cost it used to.
We don’t hold on to a decision just because it was successful at the time. When a core assumption changes, we’re willing to go back and ask whether it’s still the right call. LLMs changed one of the core assumptions behind our 2020 decision, so we reevaluated our mobile stack from first principles.
What we found led us back to native.
Why switch back to native
We decided to switch from native to React Native in 2020 for three reasons:
Stop building the same features twice
Allow developers to work across the stack
Spend less time chasing feature parity and more time shipping value
React Native consistently delivered these benefits. We found ourselves spending a significant amount of time and resources on optimizing performance, improving key foundational areas in React Native, and keeping up with framework updates and external dependencies, but these were acceptable tradeoffs. The benefits of using React Native far outweighed the investments we had to make in these areas.
Shopify has been using LLMs to build software since 2021 (one year before ChatGPT!). Initially, we used them to implement features, investigate and fix bugs, and review code. As the models improved, so did the complexity of the work we trusted them to take on. By late 2025, they were no longer just helping us write code faster. They were capable of making us question whether building software twice still meant doing twice the work.
We decided to reevaluate our mobile tech stack and started prototyping to see whether our technology choices still held up. We rebuilt several core parts of our biggest apps in Swift and Kotlin using LLMs and were surprised by how well it worked. Agents:
Could implement a feature on Android using the iOS version as a reference, and vice versa
Helped developers ramp up and contribute effectively outside their primary stack
Dramatically reduced the cost of maintaining parity between platforms through shared specifications, tests, and review checkpoints
Native still means building and maintaining software on two platforms, that cost has not disappeared. What changed is that agents can now do enough of the implementation, translation, testing, and review work that it’s no longer the deciding factor it was in 2020.
React Native apps can be fast. Ours are. We are making this change because agents have reduced the advantages of sharing implementation, while the advantages of building for each platform remain. Native keeps us closer to platform capabilities and first-party tooling, with fewer framework and dependency layers between our code and the platform.
The future of our React Native open-source libraries
Before we get into how we’re migrating, we want to make sure we do this transition cleanly. From the beginning, we wanted to contribute back to React Native to make it better. We’ve published open-source libraries that have become the top choice in their respective categories. We’re grateful for the incredible reception from the community and are committed to making sure this is a smooth transition with no surprises.
React Native Skia
Shopify will continue sponsoring this through the end of 2026, and
William Candillon
will continue working on it beyond that. He will fork the repo in the coming months and start publishing the library under a new name. The original repo will be archived when this transition is complete. We’ll post updates along the way so that everyone has ample time to migrate. If your app relies on this library, please consider sponsoring it.
FlashList
This library gets ~2M downloads/week and has become the default way to render high-performance lists in React Native. Given how important it is for the ecosystem, Shopify will continue to fix critical issues that break compatibility. We’re currently in discussions with several companies about taking on long-term stewardship of FlashList. If you’re interested, reach out to me
here
.
Restyle
Restyle has a smaller user base than our other libraries, so we're archiving this repo. We'll keep it working through the end of 2026, then stop maintaining it.

data.title: Show HN: The same nine streaming subscriptions cost $702/year more than in 2021
data.author: honestlyranked
data.article_summary: 文章比较了美国9项主流流媒体服务在2021年3月与2026年9月的价格。月费总额从95.91美元升至154.41美元，涨幅61%，年支出增加702美元，达到1852.92美元。其中Apple TV+涨幅最高（200%），其次是Disney+（138%）和Peacock（100%）；HBO Max涨幅最低（23%）。文章依据各次调价记录，强调流媒体涨价已日趋频繁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：流媒体及订阅软件价格上涨的真实性、价值变化与消费策略，同时延伸到内容网站的“LLM生成感”设计问题。

不同观点：
• 价格上涨应谨慎解读：有人指出“每年多702美元”缺乏基准，2021年总成本约1150.92美元，实际为五年上涨61%；还应纳入通胀、逐年涨幅及各平台差异。Apple TV+由4.99美元涨至14.99美元，增幅远高于YouTube Premium的33%。  
• 上涨具有合理背景：部分服务早期采用不可持续的低价吸引用户，且多年亏损；Disney+、HBO Max等直到近年才实现或接近盈利。  
• 用户价值感下降：平台碎片化、目录变浅、广告增加、设备限制和功能分级，使消费者认为“价格上涨但体验变差”，只是从一家有线公司变成几十家。  
• 消费方式存在分歧：有人认为普通用户只订一两个服务，按内容轮换，实际负担未必上涨61%；也有人拒绝订阅，选择购买CD/蓝光以获得长期所有权，或转向盗版。  
• 替代方案：PBS Passport被认为是高性价比选择；部分用户要求跨平台授权、制作与发行分离，否则只保留一个订阅或完全不付费。  
• 软件订阅也有类似问题：涨价、功能下放、高昂“按席位”收费促使用户自建软件。

补充讨论：有评论质疑文章和署名作者可能由LLM批量生成，认为其分析像“20分钟生成的内容”，并批评网站采用千篇一律的AI审美；另有人好奇这种“vibe coded”设计未来是否会成为潮流。

• 上涨具有合理背景：部分服务早期采用不可持续的低价吸引用户，且多年亏损；Disney+、HBO Max等直到近年才实现或接近盈利。  
• 用户价值感下降：平台碎片化、目录变浅、广告增加、设备限制和功能分级，使消费者认为“价格上涨但体验变差”，只是从一家有线公司变成几十家。  
• 消费方式存在分歧：有人认为普通用户只订一两个服务，按内容轮换，实际负担未必上涨61%；也有人拒绝订阅，选择购买CD/蓝光以获得长期所有权，或转向盗版。  
• 替代方案：PBS Passport被认为是高性价比选择；部分用户要求跨平台授权、制作与发行分离，否则只保留一个订阅或完全不付费。  
• 软件订阅也有类似问题：涨价、功能下放、高昂“按席位”收费促使用户自建软件。

补充讨论：有评论质疑文章和署名作者可能由LLM批量生成，认为其分析像“20分钟生成的内容”，并批评网站采用千篇一律的AI审美；另有人好奇这种“vibe coded”设计未来是否会成为潮流。

data.author: mmastrac

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软将 Rust 提升为 Tier-1，并推进 MSVC 后端、C/C++ 互操作及自动化迁移，引发对 Rust 成熟度、生态采用和技术实现的讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极认可**：认为 Rust 已是成熟、严肃的系统编程语言，微软及其他操作系统厂商的支持将增强其可信度；内存安全有助于减少漏洞（微软称约70% CVE与内存安全有关），并可能降低内存占用。  
• **生态与战略意义**：Rust 的重点已从“全面重写”转向融入现有生态，尤其是 C++、Python、JavaScript 互操作；微软、DARPA还在探索自动将大量 C 代码转换为 Rust。  
• **开发者体验认可**：Rust 的高性能、类型系统和内存安全使其适合高层应用及底层开发；有人认为它比 Zig、Odin 更成熟。  
• **采用障碍与质疑**：C++ 代码积累巨大，渐进式集成和可靠的互操作仍是普及关键；有人质疑既然是 Tier-1，为何 Visual Studio 尚未提供完整支持，尤其是调试功能。  
• **技术细节关注**：讨论集中于 Rust-C++ 集成、MSVC 后端是否替代 LLVM，以及相关组件能否对外开放；初步测试称性能与 LLVM 相当。  
• **怀疑或调侃**：有人认为该消息影响有限，也有人以 AI 将取代传统编程等说法讽刺其现实意义。

Guest Post: Rust Is Tier-1 Language at Microsoft
September 10, 2026
/
Victor Ciura
By now it’s no surprise that Rust is of strategic importance to Microsoft. From bold mission statements when Azure CTO Mark Russinovich outlined our future strategy for native code, to millions of dollars invested by Microsoft into supporting the Rust Project, over the following years. Watch
Mark’s keynote
from last year’s RustConf to get a glimpse of some of our core projects powered by Rust.
Today, Rust sits among C++, C#, and TypeScript as one of the best-supported languages for internal development at Microsoft. This “Tier-1 language” engineering status for Rust means giving internal teams a paved path from local development to production: secure toolchain builds, productive developer tooling, quality workflows, deep platform integration, and compliance with the SDL requirements Microsoft software must meet.
The Windows platform and MSVC have co-evolved for decades, as C and C++ have been the building blocks of our dev platform. As MSVC and Windows develop innovations, we need to ensure that these features and functionality are available across both C++ and Rust, and that we have
seamless interoperability
between them.
MSVC
is
the native platform compiler for Windows, and Rust needs to participate fully in that ecosystem as its usage grows across Microsoft: from firmware and drivers, kernel and hypervisors, to microservices and apps. This is extremely important in hybrid Rust/C++ projects. One of our most important investments towards this goal is
rustc_codegen_utc
.
Introducing
rustc_codegen_utc
rustc_codegen_utc
is an alternative code generation backend for rustc, in the same architectural family as
rustc_codegen_llvm
,
rustc_codegen_gcc
and
rustc_codegen_cranelift
. It plugs into the same backend interface and connects rustc’s shared compiler machinery to the MSVC backend (aka “
UTC
“).
It participates in a broader platform ecosystem strategy to support:
High compatibility with the Windows tooling eco-system and ABI
Binary hardening and code security features
Post-link compliance, analysis, and servicing (including Hotpatch)
Seamless Rust/C++ interop for hybrid projects
Cross-language inlining, optimization, and
SPGO
(Sample Profile Guided Optimization)
Debugging and crash-dump analysis
Profiling, diagnostics, and coverage
These capabilities and workflows have been built over many years with the MSVC tech-stack. Connecting rustc to that backend lets Rust build on the same platform investment, with
perfect compatibility
out of the box, rather than requiring a parallel implementation of every Windows-specific capability.
The result is a
unified
code generation platform for Rust and C++ on Windows.
Native platform evolution for Rust and C++
Production software at Microsoft moves through extensive security and quality workflows. Rust has become a Tier-1 language at Microsoft, but C++ still dominates after decades of development. Using a
unified
codegen platform will minimize both maintenance and evolution costs for us. MSVC and Windows continue to innovate. New code generation capabilities, security features, diagnostics, and servicing technologies are added all the time.
With rustc_codegen_utc, those investments land on a common foundation for both C++ and Rust. That matters operationally because it reduces duplicated engineering, but it also matters strategically: Rust participates directly in Microsoft’s Windows-native engineering ecosystem.
This is especially valuable for hybrid Rust/C++ projects, and many systems will use both languages for years to come. A shared backend creates the
foundation
for both sides of those systems to participate equally in all development workflows.
This alignment is one of the main reasons rustc_codegen_utc exists. It allows Rust to meet the engineering expectations of the environment where Microsoft teams already build, validate, diagnose, and service Windows software.
A stronger Rust and C++ interop foundation
On other platforms, if a hybrid Rust/C++ project builds its C++ code with Clang, both languages can already reach the same LLVM code generation platform. rustc_codegen_utc creates the same shared-backend opportunity for Windows-native C++ projects where MSVC is the native platform compiler.
Codegen, platform quirks, ABI, EH and post-link tooling are only
half
of the interop challenge. High-fidelity language-level interop, FFI contracts, bindings, language semantics differences… and build systems are just

data.author: jacquesm

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 OpenAI“是否允许使用个人内容训练”的设置是否真实有效、是否会被重新启用，以及用户应如何保护隐私展开。

不同观点：
• **怀疑设置形同虚设**：有人认为公司过去忽视版权方要求，因此没有理由相信这个复选框会真正生效；也有人直接怀疑即使选择“不训练”，公司也未必遵守。  
• **怀疑是技术故障而非故意行为**：有评论指出可能存在“乐观更新”或后端保存失败，界面显示关闭但实际未生效；也有人发现该选项只写入本地存储，刷新或新建标签页后可能不起作用，建议用开发者工具核实。  
• **用户经历不一致**：有人表示关闭数月后仍保持关闭，也有人从未设置却发现默认是“不允许训练”，说明可能存在地区、账户或版本差异。  
• **认为应采取更正式的退出方式**：建议通过隐私页面提交正式“隐私请求/退出申请”，并完整记录设置状态，以便日后进行法律主张或举证。  
• **对公司动机的争议**：部分人认为反复重置可能是有意制造“用户已同意”的漏洞；另一部分认为更可能是软件维护失误、更新导致配置丢失。也有人认为两种情况可能同时存在。  
• **更广泛的信任批评**：评论者警告不要向公司提供财务、健康、心理等高度敏感信息，并建议改用开放权重模型或竞争产品。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“设置失效”究竟是蓄意规避用户选择，还是普通技术缺陷；目前评论仅提供个人经历和推测，尚无确定证据。

data.author: thelastgallon
data.article_summary: 日立将在日本推出采用天然制冷剂CO₂的Y系列EcoCute热泵热水器，370升和460升型号将于2026年11月起陆续上市，分别适合3—5人和4—6人家庭。新品强化白天电价及光伏联动能源管理，支持HEMS，并提供五年厂家保修。效率参数及技术架构尚未公布，整体更像现有平台升级。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕日本CO₂热泵热水器（EcoCute）的节能效果、运行方式、环保性、安全性及海外普及前景展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **节能与削峰优势**：日本用户分享称，配合分时电价，热水器在低价、光伏发电时运行，并避开傍晚高价时段，使全电住宅的能源支出低于原先“燃气+电”的小公寓；热泵效率约为电阻加热的4—5倍。  
• **智能与使用体验**：设备可循环浴缸热水、调节水温、远程预约，并依据光伏和天气预测运行，被认为兼具舒适性和需求侧储能价值。有人指出，普通电热水器配合数字温控和混水阀，也能实现“热水电池”效果。  
• **CO₂制冷剂的环境价值**：CO₂（R744）全球变暖潜能值为1，较传统含氟制冷剂环保，泄漏影响相对小；但其技术并非新发明，因需要高压，住宅市场应用较少。  
• **成本、市场与技术担忧**：日本产品被赞赏为安静、耐用、高效，但价格偏高；评论者担心海外产品可能更便宜却噪音大、寿命短、效率低。美国、澳大利亚市场仍较小众。  
• **住宅改造方向**：有人期待CO₂空气—水热泵用于老房、铸铁暖气和水暖系统，认为PEX管道、分区控制及ERV更适合高效改造。

补充讨论：有人担心CO₂泄漏导致窒息风险；另有评论澄清“tariff”指收费标准而非关税，并质疑文章未说明JIS效率指标的具体含义。

Technology & Products

Hitachi launches CO2 heat pump water heaters with solar-friendly tariff controls
Hitachi has introduced its Y-series EcoCute CO2 heat pump water heaters in Japan, with 370-liter and 460-liter models set to launch from November 2026.
The upgraded range adds expanded support for daytime electricity tariffs and PV-linked energy management, alongside a five-year manufacturer warranty.
By
Emiliano Bellini
07 Sep 2026
Technology & Products
Heat pumps
Residential
Image: Hitachi Global Life Solutions
Advertisement
Hitachi Global Life Solutions, a unit of Japanese technology conglomerate
Hitachi
, has announced a new series of residential EcoCute heat pump water heaters for the Japanese market, with sales set to begin progressively in November 2026.
The new Y series uses natural refrigerant carbon dioxide (CO2) and is available in several configurations. At the top of the range are the BHP-FV37YD and BHP-FV46YD, two fully automatic models featuring direct mains-pressure hot-water delivery. They have storage capacities of 370 liters and 460 liters, respectively.
The 370-liter model is designed for households of around three to five people, while the 460-liter unit is aimed at households of four to six people.
Hitachi has not yet disclosed full efficiency specifications for the two new models. Their predecessors, the BHP-FV37WD and BHP-FV46WD, have annual hot-water and heat-retention efficiency ratings under Japanese Industrial Standards (JIS) of 4.2 and 4.1, respectively. The 370-liter predecessor uses a BHP-HAV45W heat pump unit, while the 460-liter version uses a BHP-HAV60W unit.
The manufacturer has not indicated whether the Y-series models feature a new compressor, refrigerant circuit or heat-exchanger architecture. Based on the specifications disclosed to date, the products appear to be an upgrade of Hitachi’s existing EcoCute platform rather than a new heat pump design.
One of the main changes in the Y series is expanded compatibility with Japanese electricity tariffs that encourage consumers to shift electricity consumption to daytime hours.
Some Japanese utilities have introduced tariffs designed to encourage daytime water heating as growing volumes of solar generation enter the grid. Hitachi said Y-series owners will be able to select supported electricity contracts through the water heater’s remote controller, while other tariffs can be configured manually.
The company said the new tariff-setting functionality is intended for electricity plans that encourage daytime consumption, including tariffs designed for households with PV systems.
The Y series also supports Hitachi’s home energy management system (HEMS) through a HEMS connection adapter and wireless LAN adapter.
HEMS connectivity is not new to Hitachi’s high-efficiency EcoCute products. The preceding BHP-FV37WD and BHP-FV46WD models already supported connected energy-management functions, including Echonet Lite compatibility and solar-powered water-heating operation. The main energy-management change in the Y series therefore appears to be expanded support for utility tariff structures rather than the introduction of HEMS connectivity itself.
Hitachi is also introducing a five-year manufacturer warranty for the Y series. The warranty covers the heat pump unit, hot-water storage unit, specified consumable components, remote controller, wireless LAN adapter and HEMS adapter.

data.author: andygcook
data.article_summary: Bending Spoons宣布以企业价值13.55亿美元收购协作平台Miro，连同净现金股权价值约17.9亿美元；部分Miro股东将把2.95亿美元收益投资于Bending Spoons新股。交易预计2026年第四季度完成，待监管批准。Miro拥有约4亿付费用户、25万家客户及约6亿美元年经常性收入，收购后将重点提升性能、可靠性和功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bending Spoons收购协作白板工具Miro引发的产品价值、收购动机及后续影响讨论。

不同观点：
• 产品价值存疑：有人误以为讨论的是视频播放器Miro；部分用户认为Miro适合制作演示文稿图表，但虚拟白板常让人花更多时间整理画布，而非完成工作；也有人认为它既不像白板、设计软件，也不像项目管理工具，难以理解其高估值。  
• 产品仍有实用性：有用户表示Miro“相当不错”，并承认它是成熟的视觉协作平台；FigJam等产品的出现也说明虚拟白板曾是明显趋势。  
• 对Bending Spoons持负面态度：评论担心其收购后会通过涨价、升级提示和暗黑模式榨取用户，并裁撤原团队、优先追求现金流，导致产品“劣化”。有人以Komoot、Eventbrite、Meetup等前收购产品的经历作为依据。  
• 对交易本身的疑问：Miro被指可能以约十倍下调的估值出售，评论者好奇创始人和员工是否能套现，以及一家成熟公司为何被迫出售；另有人质疑收购资金是否来自其他被收购公司的收益，并询问“10万美元ARR”是否为笔误。

补充讨论：评论整体偏悲观，但也有“意大利式退出”等调侃；争议焦点在于Miro的实际产品价值，以及Bending Spoons会否重演激进商业化和“榨干用户”的做法。

49643848.article_content:
Milan, Italy—September 10, 2026 |
Bending Spoons S.p.A. (NASDAQ: BSP) has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Miro at an enterprise value of $1.355 billion. Together with Miro’s net cash, this implies an equity value of approximately $1.79 billion. In connection with the all-cash transaction, certain Miro shareholders have agreed to invest $295 million of their proceeds into newly issued Bending Spoons equity. The acquisition, including the investment, is subject to customary closing conditions and approvals, including regulatory approvals.
“It's a privilege, and no small responsibility, to welcome a product that over 250,000 organizations have integrated into their workflows,” said Luca Ferrari, Bending Spoons CEO and co-founder. “Miro has grown to around $600 million in annual recurring revenue, nearly 90% from business and enterprise customers. After closing, we plan to invest substantially in the fundamentals that its customers value: performance, reliability, and functionality that supports critical collaborative work. We acquire businesses with the intention of owning and operating them for the long term, and Miro will be no exception.”
“We started Miro fifteen years ago to give teams one place to think together and bring ideas to life. It has become something more: an AI-first workspace that teams run their most important work through,” said Andrey Khusid, CEO and co-founder of Miro. “Nearly 4 million paying users depend on it, across every industry and region we serve, including more than 750 customers with over $100,000 in annual recurring revenue. The best version of Miro is still ahead of us. Partnering with Bending Spoons lets us deliver on that vision with ambition, for the customers who count on us. I’m deeply grateful to all Mironeers, partners, users, customers, and investors who have been part of Miro’s journey over the last fifteen years. Miro would not be what it is today without you, and I’m excited to see what will be built in this next chapter.”
Miro would be the latest renowned product to join Bending Spoons. Last week, Bending Spoons completed the acquisition of Airtable.
Details of the Proposed Transaction
Under the terms of the agreement, which was unanimously approved by the boards of directors of Bending Spoons and Miro, Bending Spoons will acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of Miro.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. Until the transaction closes, both companies will continue to operate independently.
Legal Counsel and Financial Advisors
Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal counsel to Bending Spoons. Ernst & Young LLP and EY Advisory S.p.A. are providing financial and tax due diligence services while McDermott Will & Schulte Studio Legale Associato is acting as Italian tax counsel to Bending Spoons. BNP Paribas and J.P. Morgan are acting as co-financial advisors to Bending Spoons.
Goodwin Procter LLP is serving as legal counsel and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Miro.
About Bending Spoons
Bending Spoons is built on the conviction that operational excellence enables efficient growth through acquisitions. It acquires digital businesses, implements deep transformations and ongoing optimizations to sustainably expand earnings, and reinvests in additional acquisitions, thereby continuing the compounding cycle. The company has executed this strategy for more than a decade and, to date, has never sold a material business.
Bending Spoons strives to envision the most successful version of an acquired business, and works to close the gap between its current state and that vision as quickly and completely as possible.
The transformation is typically deep and entails reorganizing teams, overhauling technology, redesigning user interfaces, accelerating product development, and enhancing marketing and monetization. AI is often both a central component of the vision and a key tool in implementing the transformation.
Bending Spoons’ performance is driven by its Platform—comprising its people, proprietary technologies, and proprietary data—and reflects an intense focus on achieving exceptional talent density, cultural strength, and technical capabilities.
Bending Spoons’ main businesses include Airtable, AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Tractive, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.
About Miro
Miro is the AI Innovation Workspace that brings teams and AI together to plan, co-create, and build the next big thing, faster. Serving more than 100 million users across 250,000 customers, Miro empowers cross-functional teams to progress from early discovery through final delivery on a shared, AI-first canvas. With the canvas as the prompt, Miro’s collaborative workflows keep teams in the flow of work, scale shifts in ways of working, and drive organization-wide transformation. To learn more, visit https://miro.com.

data.title: What algorithm did Windows XP use to choose your initial user picture?
data.author: soheilpro
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows 内部一个“随机选取文件/项目”的看似简单问题，实际涉及随机性、遍历成本、内存占用及边界情况处理。

不同观点：
• **严谨算法派**：认为不能简单统计文件数后随机索引，目录内容可能变化、文件数可能超过限制或出现删除/权限错误等情况，因此需要更周全的遍历和随机抽样策略。评论者赞叹微软对细节和边界情况的考虑。  
• **快速实用派**：认为实际工作中常会因时间和预算压力，直接统计特定模式文件、随机选索引，或先把最多100个文件名存入数组再随机选择；这种方案更直观，代价是额外内存或缺乏严格采样。  
• **质疑复杂度派**：有人认为只需遇到第一个匹配项就返回，或用用户名首字符配合 `rand/mod` 即可；也有人质疑为何文件系统没有直接返回目录文件数量的接口，以及“100”的上限过低。争议核心是：需求究竟要求真正均匀随机，还是只要足够实用的近似方案。  
• **计算机与人类直觉差异**：人从一堆东西中随手拿一个很容易，但计算机通常要遍历、计数、生成随机数，或使用蓄水池抽样，不能直接模拟人的动作。

补充讨论：评论还提到低层语言让人重新意识到字符串和数据结构分配的成本；大家称赞 Raymond Chen 的长期分享，并提供了相关源码链接，也有人调侃微软常在细节上优雅、整体产品体验却不尽如人意。

data.author: cdnsteve
data.article_summary: 这是一个面向Google L4-L6面试的算法与系统设计备考平台，涵盖数组、链表、哈希表、树、图、堆、Trie、排序、二分查找、递归、动态规划、BFS/DFS、贪心、Big-O及系统设计等16个主题。平台提供可视化学习、Python在线练习、真实题目、AI反馈、提示、学习路径和进度追踪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程学习资源（如 NeetCode/LeetCode）的价值、可负担性与实际学习意义。

不同观点：
• **高性价比观点**：dayvid认为，购买 NeetCode 或 LeetCode 订阅是回报率很高的投入，暗示其对算法学习、求职准备或能力提升非常有帮助。  
• **成本与可及性质疑**：esafak对这一说法提出讽刺，指出如果连二手书都买不起，却能负担相关“tokens”或订阅费用，且身边可能还有图书馆，那么订阅是否真有必要、是否适合所有人值得怀疑。争议焦点在于资源的实际价值与价格门槛。  
• **内容与体验认可**：desireco42表示自己并不需要该产品，但认为设计很酷，尤其喜欢霓虹色和视觉效果；同时认可动态规划等内容的学习价值，提到大学没有系统学习，后来还专门参加课程补足。

补充讨论：评论还涉及算法知识与实际工作的落差。desireco42认为动态规划等“智力型”问题很有意思，但现实工作中通常较少遇到，说明刷题/算法学习的教育价值与职场实用性之间可能存在差异。

data.title: Another researcher says OpenAI trained on conversations, then claimed breakthrou
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 是否使用用户对话中的未公开成果训练或改进模型，以及“退出训练”、隐私、知识产权和可信度问题。

不同观点：
• 质疑与批评：有人认为“为所有人改进模型”默认开启、措辞带有诱导性，用户并不真正理解数据如何被收集；即使退出，也难证明模型未使用过相关内容。AI 公司长期被指控搜集、挪用作品，公众不应假设自己能在“人多”中保持匿名。  
• 谨慎辩护：有人指出原作者直到今年6月29日才关闭训练授权，因此不能直接断言 OpenAI“偷窃”或恶意使用；设置中已明确说明默认允许训练，争议更可能源于用户无知、公司不透明或操作失误。若确有违反退出承诺，再有充分理由追责。  
• 安全与政策提醒：应主动关闭训练选项、避免点击反馈按钮，并研究不同公司的政策。评论特别指出，某些安全审查触发的对话可能被长期保存并用于训练；代码代理还可能误搜根目录，泄露大量个人资料。开放模型提供商也未必更安全。  
• 技术与法律争议：训练可能包括预训练、模型蒸馏或用用户轨迹构建强化学习任务，泄露和复现风险各不相同；纯LLM生成内容的版权归属、法院是否要求记录全部对话，也存在争论。

补充讨论：有人呼吁 OpenAI 通过解决真正新颖且可验证的问题来建立信任；另有评论批评学术界过度相信“退出机制”。部分参与者同时反对未经链接的截图传播，认为这加剧了误读和情绪化指控。

2026-09-08
To write non-fiction, draw the trunk, then the rest of the tree
Published
2026-09-08T11:02:50Z
Daniel
– an owl mid flight I saw last summer. try drawing it.
“You should have failed this class. I’m going to make accommodations so that no student can pass next semester the same way you did.”
This is what my Ancient History II professor told me when my group and I got our final group project essay handed out. Every group would have an interview with her to get feedback on the essays and ideally congratulate students. We did get really good feedback on the essay.
She loved the essay, but while giving that feedback she almost was exclusively looking at my friend sitting on my left. Then she looked at me, and told me to thank my friend because he obviously carried me through the essay and that I should’ve failed her class so next semester the final essay would be individual.
She was kind of right
Although it was an embarrassing moment for me, I don’t blame her. What she saw was me arriving late or even sleeping through class. I’ve always had trouble staying awake when sitting in lectures ever since kindergarten. I’ve been kicked out of classes for sleeping more times than I can count. And my friend was the complete opposite: he was active in class and had no issues with arriving in time since he lived right next to the campus.
But my writing carried me anyways
On the other hand, she was oblivious to the fact that I had written that essay almost entirely by myself while my friend was copiloting a bit on the side or sleeping while I kept writing until 6am. I was the one that read and re-read the full bibliography we used for the essay. I was the one that proposed the thesis and the main ideas. I was the one that structured the essay. What she praised was
my
writing.
The single most important thing
In Spanish we have a saying: “Irse por las ramas” (to go/leave through the branches). It describes when people deviate from the topic and discuss irrelevant stuff. It has this implicit analogy that there’s a central trunk, with branches you traverse through, but that you should always be coming back to the central trunk. For every successful essay I wrote, I identified the central trunk first.
Before writing anything you
should know what you are going write about
. Seems kind of obvious but the natural impulse I’ve seen is to write similar to how we speak: without further thinking ahead for more than a moment. But the cool thing about writing is that it’s not immediate, so you have all the time to think ahead. Before you even start writing you should have decided these two things:
1. Theme
The trunk is the theme you will be writing about. This helps you ground your ideas and not get lost in the weeds.
Reader attention is key
, and if you don’t keep it focused on the theme, readers will either get lost on what you are trying to convey or worse: get bored.
Examples:
a) This post’s theme is essay/non-fiction writing
b)
Here
the theme is brainrot and vacations
c)
Here
the theme is how SOLID and Clean Code are presented
2. Thesis (optional):
The thesis is what you want to say about the topic. You will not always have one, but if you don’t have one make that a conscious decision. If there’s an opinion there always a thesis. But theses can also be implicit throughout the text.
For example in my
latest post
there’s an implicit thesis that reading, maths, nature and socializing are a cure to brainrot. An example of a post of mine that doesn’t have a thesis is
this post
where I share my earliest memories that supposedly I shouldn’t be able to remember.
As a rule of thumb, if what you are going to write is exclusively expository, narrative, descriptive, functional / transactional; then it’s
possible
that you don’t have a thesis.
But even then make it a conscious decision
because even the forms I described above can carry an implicit thesis.
Support the most important thing
Now that you have decided what you’ll be writing, make sure everything you write is in line with that. Think of it as a hierarchy where the Theme/Thesis is at the top and then you have the arguments that support your thesis. For longform writing I like to think of arguments as further mini-theses that in turn can be supported by more arguments and so on.
Arguments can be supported by:
Evidence / facts — verifiable statements
Data & statistics — quantified evidence
Expert testimony / authority — citing someone credible
Quotations & citations — letting a source speak directly
Anecdotes / personal experience — a lived instance
Case studies — one example examined in depth
Analogies & comparisons — explaining via something familiar
Cause-and-effect reasoning — showing the mechanism
Definitions — pinning down a term the argument depends on
Hypotheticals / thought experiments — invented scenarios to test a claim
Concessions — granting a limit, which strengthens credibility
Counter-arguments & rebuttals — raising the objection, then answering it

Who Do You Talk to When You’re Struggling?
Religion and politics shape whether Americans turn to a therapist, a pastor, or someone closer to home.
Ryan Burge
Sep 10, 2026
24
1
Share
Article voiceover

Audio playback is not supported on your browser. Please upgrade.
T
his post has been unlocked through a generous grant from the
Lilly Endowment
for the
Association of Religion Data Archives
(ARDA). The graphs you see here use data that is publicly available for download and analysis through link(s) provided in the text below.
Who do you talk to when you’re struggling?
When it feels like you’re carrying the weight of the world and there’s no way out of the mess you’re in—who can you turn to for an honest conversation?
I’d bet that for a lot of us, the answer is “no one.”
Many Americans are suffering in silence, without a spouse, a close friend, or even a co-worker they can lean on when times get tough. The
loneliness epidemic
has real casualties. Of that, I am absolutely sure.
I
saw a video
on Reddit a couple of weeks ago that got me thinking about this. It was posted in “
HumansBeingBros
,” a subreddit that exists to make you feel a little better about the world. A motorcyclist comes upon a man walking down the middle of the road, clearly in distress. The rider stops his bike, turns around, and engages with the man—at one point even asking if he needs a hug.
Later in the video, the two of them are sitting against a fence on the side of the road. Here’s the part I love: whoever uploaded it blurred the man’s face and captioned the moment with just a few words—”talked about his struggles.” No details. I can really appreciate that. We don’t need to know what the man was dealing with. He deserves his privacy. The video ends with the police arriving to offer him a ride home.
But it left me with a question: who can people actually talk to in an open and honest way? I’ve got some data from Pew that speaks directly to this. It’s a simple battery of questions from
American Trends Panel 142
, hosted on
the ARDA
. The preamble is straightforward: “
How comfortable would you be talking about your mental health and emotional well-being with each of the following?
” Then respondents rated several options:
Close Friends
Spouse/Partner
Immediate Family Member
Mental Health Therapist
A Co-Worker
Neighbor
Religious/Spiritual Leader
Let’s start with the share of each religious group who said they were extremely or very comfortable talking about their mental health with each of those individuals.
One thing that is crystal clear from this data is that people truly rely on their spouses or partners when it comes to being honest and open about what’s happening in their lives.
Among every religious group, the spouse scores the highest, often by a wide margin. The response levels are remarkably consistent, too: most are within a few points of 80%. An interesting outlier is the LDS community—nearly 90% say they are very or extremely comfortable sharing mental health issues with their spouse.
The other groups follow a consistent rank ordering.
Close friends, mental health therapists, and immediate family members all rank similarly, typically in the 50-60% range for most religious traditions.
At the bottom are co-workers and neighbors, who score poorly; people generally aren’t willing to be vulnerable around them.
But there was one blip in the data worth digging into: the responses regarding comfort levels with religious or spiritual leaders. For most respondents, this doesn’t rank high. Only about a third of non-evangelical Protestants, Catholics, and LDS members feel very or extremely comfortable speaking with their pastor about their struggles.
But for evangelicals, that number jumps to 56%—putting clergy in the same neighborhood as immediate family or close friends
.
That outlier led me to compare two specific options: speaking with a mental health therapist versus a member of the clergy. I wondered if certain religious groups favored one over the other. The graph below explores that comparison.
It’s clearly the case that the average person of faith feels more comfortable talking with a counselor than a member of the clergy
. Among Catholics, half feel very or extremely comfortable talking to a mental health professional, while only 33% say the same about talking to a priest. For LDS members, those numbers are 52% and 25%, respectively. (This may be related to how the LDS Church is organized, as they do not have a traditional paid clergy). Across almost every group, there’s a clear throughline: people of faith aren’t always keen on talking to their pastors about their troubles.
However, evangelicals are the exception.
They are actually slightly more comfortable talking with their pastor (56%) than with a therapist (51%) regarding their emotional well-being.

data.title: Stockfish 19
data.author: atiedebee
data.article_summary: Stockfish 19于2026年9月5日发布，相比Stockfish 18最高提升44 Elo，胜率显著增强。新版本采用通用二进制，升级SFNNv16神经网络与训练技术，移除次级网络，并支持RISC-V、LoongArch、WebAssembly及Linux大页内存。同时加强棋盘、FEN和UCI指令验证，出错后会提示并终止。项目继续由社区维护，遵循GPL开源协议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Stockfish 19 发布后的棋力、评估变化、使用体验，以及棋类引擎的历史、工具价值和未来发展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **Stockfish 19评估可能出现回归或搜索深度问题**：有人以 1999 年卡斯帕罗夫—托帕洛夫名局为例，指出同一局面在深度25时，Stockfish 18评估白方约领先3.53分，而19仅领先1.2分；到深度35才判断白胜（+6.79），因此认为19需要更深搜索才能发现胜势，可能属于回归。  
• **Stockfish 19依然更强**：有人以实战调侃“过去输给18，现在输给19，而且可能更快”，侧面支持新版棋力提升；也有人讨论旧版本在现代硬件上是否足以与最新版抗衡，认为从初始局面最终大多只能和棋。  
• **引擎应增强可解释性**：评论希望 Stockfish 能用自然语言说明推荐着法和连续变化，以帮助学习，而不是只给出分数和主变。  
• **GUI与配套资源需要更新**：有人认为相关GUI介绍过时，推荐 Nocheto、ChessMD、PyChess；也有人建议发布说明加入评估差异最大的经典或基准对局。  
• **对棋类引擎的不同态度**：部分人将引擎视为学习和挑战工具，甚至希望自己编写能击败自己的棋力程序；另一些人认为棋类思想难以迁移到现实，投入时间不如学习博弈论或娱乐。  
• **历史与AI竞争讨论**：评论回顾 Fritz、Junior、Shredder、Rybka、Crafty、AlphaZero/Leela 等引擎，认为人机对弈已不再有悬念，并提出 Stockfish 与 AlphaZero、甚至LLM从零学棋比较的设想。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是 Stockfish 19 的评估变化究竟是算法回归、搜索深度差异，还是更准确地反映局面；同时也涉及“棋力提升”与“可解释、可学习性”之间的取舍。

Today, we have the pleasure of announcing
Stockfish 19
, a new major release. As always, you can freely download it at
stockfishchess.org/download
and use it as a drop-in replacement in the
GUI of your choice
to benefit from stronger play and more accurate analysis.
Whether you can spare hours or days of CPU time, your help matters for the ongoing development of Stockfish. Find out how you can contribute at
stockfishchess.org/get-involved
. Join our
Discord server
to get in touch with the community of developers and users of the project!
Quality of Chess Play
In tests against Stockfish 18, this new release brings an Elo gain of
up to 44 points
, and wins
more than three times as many game pairs
as it loses.
Stockfish continues to set the standard for engine strength. Against the strongest competition, it consistently secures the top spot in engine championships, continuing to
dominate the field
.
Update Highlights
Universal Binaries
We have transitioned to universal binaries for our releases, simplifying the download process. These universal binaries automatically detect the features of your CPU and run the optimal code, eliminating the need to manually choose between AVX2, AVX-512, etc.
Upgraded NNUE Architecture and Training
This release introduces the SFNNv16 network architecture, reducing binary size by removing redundant threat features while increasing strength by introducing new pawn-pair features. The secondary neural network, introduced in Stockfish 16.1, has been retired, enhancing strength in positions where the small net previously underperformed.
The training process has been further improved with the introduction of new techniques, such as Quantization-Aware Training (QAT), and further parameter tweaks. These techniques have been applied to hundreds of billions of training positions, all of which have been consistently rescored using a strong
Leela
net.
Expanded Platform Support
We have added native support for RISC-V (RVV) and LoongArch (LSX/LASX), 1GB Linux huge pages, as well as WebAssembly targets. The shared-memory implementation for Linux, macOS, and BSD was also overhauled.
Strict Position Validation
We have implemented stricter validation for board positions, FEN strings, and UCI commands. The engine will now output an
info string CRITICAL ERROR
followed by the exact command and the reason it failed, and then immediately terminate the process. A good GUI will ensure you never encounter these errors.
Thank You
The Stockfish project builds on a thriving community of enthusiasts (thanks to everybody!) who contribute their expertise, time, and resources to build a free and open-source chess engine that is robust, widely available, and very strong.
We would like to express our gratitude for the 16.4k stars that light up our GitHub project. Thank you for your support and encouragement – your recognition means a lot to us. Programmers can contribute to the project either directly to
Stockfish
(C++), to
Fishtest
(HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python), to our trainer
nnue-pytorch
(C++ and Python), or to our
website
(HTML, CSS/SCSS, and JavaScript).

49599992.article_summary: Stockfish 19于2026年9月5日发布，相比Stockfish 18最高提升44 Elo，胜率显著增强。新版本采用通用二进制，升级SFNNv16神经网络与训练技术，移除次级网络，并支持RISC-V、LoongArch、WebAssembly及Linux大页内存。同时加强棋盘、FEN和UCI指令验证，出错后会提示并终止。项目继续由社区维护，遵循GPL开源协议。
49599992.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Stockfish 19 发布后的棋力、评估变化、使用体验，以及棋类引擎的历史、工具价值和未来发展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **Stockfish 19评估可能出现回归或搜索深度问题**：有人以 1999 年卡斯帕罗夫—托帕洛夫名局为例，指出同一局面在深度25时，Stockfish 18评估白方约领先3.53分，而19仅领先1.2分；到深度35才判断白胜（+6.79），因此认为19需要更深搜索才能发现胜势，可能属于回归。  
• **Stockfish 19依然更强**：有人以实战调侃“过去输给18，现在输给19，而且可能更快”，侧面支持新版棋力提升；也有人讨论旧版本在现代硬件上是否足以与最新版抗衡，认为从初始局面最终大多只能和棋。  
• **引擎应增强可解释性**：评论希望 Stockfish 能用自然语言说明推荐着法和连续变化，以帮助学习，而不是只给出分数和主变。  
• **GUI与配套资源需要更新**：有人认为相关GUI介绍过时，推荐 Nocheto、ChessMD、PyChess；也有人建议发布说明加入评估差异最大的经典或基准对局。  
• **对棋类引擎的不同态度**：部分人将引擎视为学习和挑战工具，甚至希望自己编写能击败自己的棋力程序；另一些人认为棋类思想难以迁移到现实，投入时间不如学习博弈论或娱乐。  
• **历史与AI竞争讨论**：评论回顾 Fritz、Junior、Shredder、Rybka、Crafty、AlphaZero/Leela 等引擎，认为人机对弈已不再有悬念，并提出 Stockfish 与 AlphaZero、甚至LLM从零学棋比较的设想。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是 Stockfish 19 的评估变化究竟是算法回归、搜索深度差异，还是更准确地反映局面；同时也涉及“棋力提升”与“可解释、可学习性”之间的取舍。

data.title: List of references on Sony websites to players "owning" their digital games
data.author: haunter
data.article_summary: 四名加州消费者起诉索尼，指控PlayStation商店以“购买”等措辞销售数字游戏，却未醒目说明消费者获得的只是可撤销、不可转让的使用许可，而非所有权，违反加州数字商品透明度法。索尼否认消费者会被误导，并申请强制个人仲裁或驳回案件。案件仍在审理，听证会定于2026年10月1日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕索尼数字游戏“购买是否等于拥有”、用户权利及相关诉讼策略展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 反对强制仲裁：认为个人绑定仲裁和集体诉讼豁免削弱消费者权利；30天书面退出条款虽形式上提供选择，实际上多数用户并不知情，是规避责任的设计。  
• 质疑“数字所有权不存在”：索尼称不同用户先后购买同一游戏，说明用户获得的是可撤销许可而非所有权。评论者认为这与日常“买书即拥有一份书”的理解矛盾，且索尼在“所有权”和“许可”之间选择性用词。  
• 支持数字产权改革：应确立真正的数字所有权，允许转售、脱离平台使用，并在商店关闭或商品下架后通过托管等方式继续访问；也有人主张无DRM及提供实体介质。  
• 担忧消费模式倒退：实体游戏可转售，形成“首发价—二手价”的可负担机制；数字租赁会让消费者失去转售和收藏权，强化“只能使用、不能拥有”。  
• 批评索尼诉讼策略：认为“一个人拥有后别人就不能购买”的论证荒谬，甚至可能反过来引发盗版等逻辑问题；即使胜诉，也可能损害其营销信誉。  
• 相对审慎观点：有人指出类似条款是现代商业合同的普遍现象，不应只针对索尼，并怀疑舆论是否存在过度集中或“水军”现象。

补充讨论：争议核心是数字购买的法律性质，以及平台合同能否凌驾于消费者对“购买、拥有、转售”的合理期待之上。

data.title: Show HN: What if the speed of light was 5 km/h?
data.author: dmitrybrant
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个将光速设为5公里/小时的相对论模拟公园。用户可通过移动观察速度接近光速时的长度收缩、时间膨胀、光行时延、相对论像差、特雷尔旋转、多普勒效应和相对论光束效应，并观察灯柱、摩天轮和航天器的变化。文章还说明了模拟的现实局限与操作方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“将光速大幅降低”的相对论模拟游戏，讨论其物理准确性、直观体验、模拟机制及相关科幻作品。

不同观点：
• 有人认为本作比MIT 2012年的《A Slower Speed of Light》更准确，尤其正确呈现了相对论多普勒效应的时间因素；但也有人质疑非共线洛伦兹变换产生的空间旋转（W、A组合移动后方向应改变）未被体现，以及车顶可见、移动方向反常等现象是否是程序问题。  
• 有人强调“光速很慢”取决于参考系：即使以99.999%光速前往仙女座，地球观察者仍需约1.1万年，但相对于宇宙年龄或旅行者自身时间，这并非同样漫长。  
• 有人指出光速并非可独立调节的变量，它与精细结构常数、质能关系及信息传播机制相连；因此游戏更像是“光对玩家看起来只有5英里/小时”，而非完整模拟真实物理世界。  
• 另有评论单纯欣赏游戏的教育和娱乐价值，并推荐《Velocity Raptor》、MIT旧作及相关科幻作品作为补充。

补充讨论：评论还提出若光速低于声速，将出现“先听到声音、后看到动作”的体验；同时有人希望增加移动端控制。

In this park, the speed of light is 5 kilometers per hour — a brisk walk.

The more you speed up, the more relativistic effects will become apparent:

Things to try
Accelerate by pressing the Up arrow. Your field of view begins to condense
in the direction you are traveling, and becomes blueshifted. If you look
behind you by using your mouse to turn, that field of view is redshifted
and stretched out. This is
relativistic aberration
. Press Space
to stop any motion, and observe how the field of view returns to normal.
The
lamp posts
all flash once per second of world time. Move toward a lamp
and the flashing speeds up; move away and it slows down. Also observe the timers
labeled "Your watch" and "World clock", and see time dilation in effect.
The
Ferris wheel
and
carousel
cars move at 75% of the speed of light.
They are contracted by their own motion, and you see each one at a different moment in its trip
around the circle. As the cars move around, you can see the effects of relativistic
contraction and
Terrell rotation
.
The
shuttle
near the end of the corridor runs back and forth, also attaining a speed
of 75% of the speed of light. Notice how it also contracts and undergoes Terrell rotation as it moves.
What's NOT accurate
Obviously a Ferris wheel spinning at relativistic speeds would fly apart, and if you travel through
the atmosphere at relativistic speeds, you would be vaporized instantly. Even if you travel near
the speed of light in interstellar space, you would be cooked by the cosmic microwave background radiation
blueshifted to gamma rays.
The rendering of blueshifts and redshifts is a rough approximation.
At extreme redshifts, the color fades to black. And at extreme blueshifts (past violet),
the color turns to a metallic silver to represent x-rays, then to bright white
to represent gamma rays (totally unphysical, but just to get a sense of it).

data.title: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash
data.author: Liwink
data.article_summary: DeepSeek发布新架构系列中最小模型DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash，具备原生视觉理解能力，旨在提升模型能力、推理速度与吞吐量，并为扩展至更大型模型奠定基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash的技术创新、性能与价格，以及其与其他模型和本地部署的比较。

不同观点：
• 技术透明与创新派：认为DeepSeek技术报告细节丰富、持续引入大胆架构创新，体现其可能是领先的AI实验室；相比之下，Anthropic的系统卡更偏重安全、模型福利和基准数据，技术细节不足。  
• 性能领先派：部分评测称其击败 Opus 5、Sol 5.6，可能成为开放权重模型的新标杆；也有人认为它更听从用户要求、适合作为低价备用模型。  
• 谨慎评价派：有人认为相较V4提升有限，却贵约3倍；在特定谜题评测中，Gemini 3.8 Flash仍更便宜且更强，模型还可能消耗过多推理token。  
• 成本与缓存派：缓存命中价低至每百万token 0.003美元，长程编程任务中可显著降低总成本；讨论进一步指出，未来网络传输和上下文缓存成本可能超过模型推理本身，冲击传统API模式。  
• 部署与规模担忧：模型从284B扩大到552B，虽仅约16B激活并改进KV缓存，但本地运行需要极大内存，256GB设备可能不足，因此“Flash”名不副实。  
• 使用体验问题：移动端对英文提示仍常回复中文；部分用户关注其过度思考、语言遵循和实际可靠性。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于基准成绩是否代表真实能力、价格“降低”应如何理解，以及性能提升能否抵消模型规模和部署成本。

data.author: olalonde
data.article_summary: 大型太平洋条纹章鱼（LPSO）是一种尚未正式命名的章鱼，分布于东太平洋热带海域。它们性情群居，可形成最多40只的群体，具有独特的亲密交配、终生多次繁殖和结伴生活行为。体色多样，常见棕白条纹斑点。主要捕食虾、蟹、双壳类等，寿命约两年。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕大西洋条纹章鱼（LPSO）的体型、分类研究、社会行为、智能潜力及相关资料可靠性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 资料质疑：teiferer指出页面未说明体型，补充其约“网球大小”；Rygian质疑论文把危地马拉、巴拿马与加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚并列，可能是将Colombia误写为 Columbia。  
• 分类研究滞后：TulliusCicero惊讶该物种自20世纪70年代被记录后，五十多年仍未正式命名，质疑科学研究效率。  
• 社会性与繁殖：NewJazz强调其交配后不会立即死亡，猜测这可能允许亲代向幼体传授技能；listingbott进一步追问其为何从多数独居章鱼演化出群居性。  
• 智能潜力：rolfus认为头足类是最接近“外星智能”的动物，遗憾其寿命短，并设想长寿可能释放更大认知潜力。  
• 语言与趣味：drakonka欣赏“群居性”“亲密拥抱”等拟人化、富有诗意的描述；monster_truck则以玩笑方式追问遇到更大个体会怎样。  
• 科普与技术反思：diurnalist感叹人类仍不了解地球生命，主张保持谦逊，并质疑AI翻译、合成动物声音的应用价值；durakot则提到章鱼被用于个人操作系统代理项目。

补充讨论：部分评论提供旁证或联想，如条纹驱蚊的斑马说法，但与核心议题关联较弱。

The

The species was first documented in the 1970s and, being fairly new to scientific observation, has yet to be scientifically described. Because of this, LPSO has no official scientific name.

[
8

The LPSO has been found to favor the tropical waters of the Eastern Pacific.
[
2

Appearance
[
edit
]
LPSO exhibits three main body color patterns that include completely pale, completely dark brown, and a dark brown and white pattern that is referred to as "stripe-bar-spot".
[
2
]
When displaying the stripe-bar-spot body color pattern, LPSO is observed to have bar and stripe patterns that alternate between brown and white across its head and mantle, and dark brown with white spots over its arm, crown, and arms.
[
2

The pattern can serve as a unique identifier as it varies among individuals.

Habitat and distribution
[
edit
]
LPSO has been documented in many locations throughout the tropics of the Eastern Pacific. Specimens have been located in the Bay of Panama, Panama, Guatemala, Magdelena Bay, Baja Sur, Mexico, the northern Pacific coast of Colombia, and Nicaragua.
[
2
]
LPSO seems to prefer denning in areas with soft muddy substrates or a mix of mud and sand, ranging in depth from 7m to 100m.
[
2
]
The species has also been observed to form colonies of up to 40 close-living individuals.
[
4
]
These colonies of LPSO construct dens within 1m of one another and live in the same general area for the span of their lives.
[
4
]
Mating
[
edit
]
LPSO is known in particular for its display of mating behaviors that are vastly different from most octopus species. While most octopuses use either "distance mating" (when the male places his
hectocotylus
into the female's mantle from a safe distance) or a mounting position,
[
13
]
[
14

]
LPSO uses a more intimate approach. Typically, a brooding female that is ready to mate exhibits an entirely pale body color pattern while the male exhibits a high contrast stripe-bar-spot body color pattern.
[
2
]
Once the male and female LPSO decide to mate, they join in a beak-to-beak position, embracing in an entanglement of arms.
[
2
]
Unlike some species of octopus, female LPSO are not
cannibalistic
during mating and are rather gentle, leaving only surface level sucker marks as a result of the beak-to-beak embrace.
[
2
]
Pair bonding has been observed in LPSO through behaviors such as food and den sharing.
[
2
]
Brooding
[
edit
]
Unlike most octopus species, LPSO can spawn multiple times throughout the span of their life.
[
2
]
Eggs are laid in pairs within the den and the female tends to them until they hatch, running the tips of her arms over them to maintain the health of the eggs.
[
2
]
Once hatched from the egg, the offspring are
pelagic
until adulthood.
[
16
]
Hunting
[
edit
]
LPSO has been observed to prey upon a variety of shellfish including
shrimp
,
stomatopods
,
crabs
, and
bivalves
.
[
2
]
They use hunting methods of stalking, chasing, and ambush depending on the prey item in question.
[
2
]
When eating bivalves, smaller prey is either crushed or pulled apart, while holes are drilled into larger prey.
[
2
]
When hunting shrimp, LPSO carefully extends its arm, suckers positioned outward, to touch and capture the shrimp.
[
2
]
When hunting crabs, LPSO uses an ambush method, pouncing directly onto the crab for capture.
[
2
]
Lifespan
[
edit
]
LPSO live about two years.
[
3
]
Like most octopus species, LPSO goes through a stage of
senescence
, which marks the approach of death.
[
2
]
Senescence in LPSO has been observed to be longer for females and shorter for males.

2

data.article_summary: 本文介绍开源Fortran-90软件DDSCAT 7.2及其离散偶极子近似（DDA）理论与使用方法。该程序可模拟任意几何、非均匀及各向异性目标对电磁波的散射、吸收和近场分布，支持孤立目标及一、二维周期结构，并提供多种目标模型、MPI/OpenMP/MKL并行计算和近场读取工具。在折射率差不大、尺寸参数小于约25时可获得较准确结果。

Title:
User Guide for the Discrete Dipole Approximation Code DDSCAT 7.2
Authors:
Bruce T. Draine
(Princeton Univ.),
Piotr J. Flatau
(UCSD)
View a PDF of the paper titled User Guide for the Discrete Dipole Approximation Code DDSCAT 7.2, by Bruce T. Draine (Princeton Univ.) and Piotr J. Flatau (UCSD)
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
DDSCAT 7.2 is a freely available open-source Fortran-90 software package applying the discrete dipole approximation (DDA) to calculate scattering and absorption of electromagnetic waves by targets with arbitrary geometries and complex refractive index. The targets may be isolated entities (e.g., dust particles), but may also be 1-d or 2-d periodic arrays of "target unit cells", which can be used to study absorption, scattering, and electric fields around arrays of nanostructures.
The DDA approximates the target by an array of polarizable points. The theory of the DDA and its implementation in DDSCAT is presented in Draine (1988) and Draine & Flatau (1994), and its extension to periodic structures in Draine & Flatau (2008). Efficient near-field calculations are enabled following Flatau & Draine (2012). DDSCAT 7.2 allows accurate calculations of electromagnetic scattering from targets with size parameters 2*pi*aeff/lambda < 25 provided the refractive index m is not large compared to unity (|m-1| < 2). DDSCAT 7.2 includes support for MPI, OpenMP, and the Intel Math Kernel Library (MKL).
DDSCAT 7.2 supports calculations for a variety of target geometries (e.g., ellipsoids, regular tetrahedra, rectangular solids, finite cylinders, hexagonal prisms, etc.). Target materials may be both inhomogeneous and anisotropic. It is straightforward for the user to import new target geometries into the code. DDSCAT 7.2 calculates total cross sections for absorption and scattering and selected elements of the Mueller scattering intensity matrix for specified orientation of the target relative to the incident wave, and for specified scattering directions. DDSCAT 7.2 calculates E throughout a user-specified rectangular volume containing the target. A Fortran-90 code READNF to read E and P from files created by DDSCAT 7.2 is included in the distribution.

data.article_summary: 文章介绍 Ampbase 直接以 Tigris 对象存储作为数据层，不使用关系数据库，而是在其基础上自行实现唯一约束、事务、索引和历史表等数据库能力。系统通过分层存储组织与客户数据，利用键结构实现相关功能，并采用 Protobuf 提升性能、避免迁移；客户隔离由基础设施和凭证权限保证。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• 质疑实用性：文章缺乏动机，像“用两把椅子搭办公桌”；自行实现唯一约束、事务、索引和历史记录属于重复造轮子，可能浪费开发者时间。  
• 质疑功能完整性：数据库能力不止四项，还包括可串行化、复制、物化视图、过程、锁和访问控制；评论者认为最终可能仍需迁移到Postgres。  
• 质疑工程风险：缓存一旦承担关键职责，本质上就是一个未备份、故障可能静默的数据库；基于FoundationDB却不直接使用其事务、范围读取等能力，反而增加缓存和并发处理复杂度。  
• 支持有限场景：若没有强记录级并发需求，平文件或对象存储更简单、便宜、易维护；可通过数据模型设计应对基本需求。  
• 质疑创新性与质量：Iceberg、Delta Lake等已有类似能力；“某某就够用”的标题常被认为夸大，文章还被批评为AI生成内容。

49618450.article_content:
Context
Tigris makes object storage using a database engine we built on top of
FoundationDB: a distributed key-value store. JP, the founder of Ampbase, uses a
control plane on Tigris with no database underneath it, and today he's going
over which database behaviors he had to build himself and what that cost.
Thanks JP!
Last time on
the Ampbase blog
I talked
about all the database engines that we don't use and promised to follow up
explaining what we actually do. We don't use a relational database. We use
Tigris as the storage layer directly, and implement the few database behaviors
we actually need on top of the two primitives it gives us. Yeah, yeah, I know;
"we didn't need a database" is a catchy title that usually happens about eight
(8) months before the inevitable next post being "how we tucked our tail between
our legs and moved to Postgres".
In practice, when you reach for a database engine you're actually reaching for
four basic features: unique constraints, transactions, indices, and history
tables. In order to use Tigris' global object storage as a database, we had to
implement all of these primitives ourselves. Today I'm going to peel back the
curtain and show you how those primitives work so you can understand what
actually goes into your database engine of choice.
What's actually stored
​
Everything lives in two layers of buckets.
A global
directory
bucket holds the list of organizations, and every
organization gets a bucket of its own. Four of those keys are doing a job a
database would normally do for you, so they're labelled here and picked apart in
the next section:
FIG 01
the two layers, and which primitive each key implements
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ directory bucket                         one, global │
│                                                      │
│   orgs/{org_id}/                                     │
│     metadata.json                                    │
│     members/{sha256(email)}.json                     │
the index
│     billing.json                                     │
the compare-and-swap target
│     channels/{channel_id}/metadata.json              │
│     api-tokens/{token_id}.json                       │
│     events/audit/{event_ulid}.pb                     │
the audit log
│   org-ops/queue.pb                                   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
provider credentials reach this one, and only this one
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ org bucket                          one per customer │
│                                                      │
│   channel-slugs/{slug}.json                          │
the unique constraint
│   channel-{channel_id}/                              │
│     config-meta/{config_id}.json                     │
│     config-versions/{version_ulid}.json              │
the history table
│     bundle-meta/{bundle_id}.pb                       │
│     bundle-versions/{bundle_id}/{version_ulid}.pb    │
│     active-config.pb                                 │
a pointer, overwritten in place
│     events/{event_ulid}.json                         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
that customer's scoped keys reach this one, and nothing else
We started out writing everything as JSON objects to each customer's bucket.
After a while we started adopting more and more features to our API with
protobuf options
so
we can
define validation alongside the schema definition
among other things. Marshaling and unmarshaling all the JSON got more expensive
than we thought, so we switched to using Protocol Buffers directly. Our database
handles both formats so if records predate the protobuf migration, everything
loads as expected.
By using Protobuf, we eliminate the whole problem of managing a database layer:
migrations, connections, schemas. The only downside is that Protobuf field names
are forever, but to be fair it's about equally as painful to change column names
in Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite.
The naive way to create a bucket per customer would be to make a bucket per
customer, all in the same $bigcloud account and create a new account every time
you hit a quota limit. Or have one bucket with prefixes to get around the
per-account bucket limit, and rely on complexity in the IAM policy to enforce
isolation. All of this sounded rather dull, and Tigris has a
Partner Integration Program
for exactly this shape anyway. One call to it creates a Tigris organization for
that customer, its bucket, and a set of access keys scoped to it. We hold a
provider identity; each customer is an organization underneath it, with strong
isolation.
Isolation is baked into the infrastructure layer: no
WHERE org_id = ?
to
forget in your app code, because the credentials that reach one customer's data
cannot address anyone else's. As someone who has built a few platforms that
managed databases in the past, this is the part that most people mess up.

data.title: Show HN: Art – draw one stroke, let symmetry complete it
data.author: cyb0rg0
data.article_summary: 这是一款曼陀罗图案绘制工具。用户可设置配色方式、对称数量、密度、画笔与墨水效果（实线、发光、渐变、喷洒等），并调整透明度、镜像和对称锁定。工具支持生成曼陀罗、重新着色、撤销、清空及下载 PNG；重新着色会保留图形结构并重新运行配色方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款基于镜像/径向对称生成图案的绘画工具，讨论集中在使用体验、界面优化、技术概念及类似作品。

不同观点：
• **积极体验**：多数评论认为绘画过程令人满足、催眠且容易沉浸，有人不知不觉玩了10–15分钟；笔刷大小、金属质感、渐变等选项也受到认可。  
• **界面与交互问题**：有人建议将控制面板放在画布侧边或固定在底部，并让输出与输入并排，以实现“零滚动”。现有布局导致用户反复上下滚动。另有用户反馈滚动选择颜色时，画布会撤销上一笔，疑似交互或状态保存 bug。  
• **概念与审美讨论**：有人质疑仅具备径向对称是否足以称为“曼陀罗”；也有人认为，即使作品不符合严格数学对称，艺术上的不对称本身仍具有美感。  
• **类似工具与怀旧联想**：评论者将其与 WeaveSilk、Deluxe Paint、Koala Pad、Krita、Open Brush 以及《纪念碑谷》中的镜像绘画功能联系起来，说明该创意有较长的工具和游戏传统。  
• **拓展需求**：有用户期待推出移动端应用，也有人分享了自己制作的类似儿童绘画工具。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是“曼陀罗”的定义，以及严格数学对称与艺术表现之间的关系；整体上评论以赞赏为主，批评集中在可用性和操作 bug。

data.title: Thanks to Siri Recaps, your Apple Watch is always listening
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 文章介绍苹果为Apple Watch推出的Siri Recaps和Live Rewind：前者实时分析日常对话并生成摘要，后者可转录最近15秒音频。苹果称音频不录制、不存储，依靠设备端及私有云处理。但作者认为，这类“始终监听”的功能即使有助于会议记录和无障碍使用，也会引发未经他人同意被监控的隐私担忧，可能重蹈智能眼镜遭抵制的覆辙。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕智能设备持续监听、录音转写与个人信息回顾功能的实用性、隐私风险及法律责任展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持或条件支持者认为，该功能可像“记忆辅助”一样，帮助用户回忆会议、人物和约定；若只处理用户本来能知道的信息、且不保存音频，价值较高，但实际隐私政策和执行仍待观察。  
• 隐私担忧者认为，持续监听可能扩大数据收集范围，甚至暗中加入监控功能；“大家早就被录了”的说法可能正在推动监听设备正常化，智能眼镜、电视和手机都可能成为类似工具。  
• 法律风险派指出，在马萨诸塞州等双重同意州，未经他人同意录音可能违法；企业或许会把责任转嫁给用户。有人曾因会议机器人遗漏同意提示而被迫下线。  
• 安全风险派担心录音、转写内容泄露，办公室可能因此禁止智能手表等设备；也有人认为既然手机、手表本就常态监听，这只是更充分利用麦克风。  
• 怀疑实用性者质疑 Siri 连英语、法语和基础听写都经常出错，转写功能可能“不可靠”；部分用户因此拒绝购买 Apple Watch，或继续使用老式 Pebble 以避免数据采集。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“是否真正不存储音频、能否有效保护第三方同意与隐私”，以及便利性是否值得承担安全、法律和认知依赖成本。

The
Apple Watch
Series 12 and
Apple
Watch Ultra 4 have landed,
along with a revolutionary folding iPhone at this year's Apple event
, but despite major advancements under the hood, the feature that is standing out to me is a software-based one.
Siri Recaps is a new Audio Intelligence feature that turns your Apple Watch into an always-listening device. The idea is that Siri Recaps, which lives on the Siri app, uses the Apple Watch's sensors to provide a summary of your day, including conversations that have taken place. It can be toggled with a schedule, or at the top of the Smart Stack.
It's a little like the
Amazon Bee
, which is a microphone attached to a smart band, which is used to capture and summarize conversations. While I can see this feature as being useful for people who attend lots of meetings (having a virtual assistant taking minutes in the background all day long could be very useful), there are understandably privacy concerns here.
Latest Videos From
TechRadar
Watch full video here:
We're told the Recaps feature doesn't record or store audio and it can't show a transcript. Instead, it processes events live as they take place, using Siri AI to turn that raw data into actionable notes, never written into permanent storage. Below is a screenshot from Apple's presentation:
(Image credit: Apple)
Your watch, like a smartphone or smart speaker, already has to always listen for a wake word (like 'Siri' or 'Alexa'), but the audio it's listening to is not logged or recorded: only interactions starting with the wake word are.
You may like
Apple's watchOS team told me what Siri AI will bring to the Apple Watch
Meta’s super-sensing AI glasses edge one step closer to reality
'The chicification of surveillance is deeply concerning' — why our tech is getting far too close (and what you can do about it)
But add an always-listening AI assistant into the mix who's taking notes on your day-to-day, including your conversations with others who may not know they're being surveilled, and suddenly Apple's latest handy feature starts to look a lot creepier. Apple's other big new Audio Intelligence feature for watches is Live Rewind, which can produce a transcript of the last 15 seconds of audio on your watch face — whether a wake word was said, or not.
I'm frankly surprised Apple even went through with this feature at this time, considering the bans and backlash other AI-powered surveillance wearables are getting.

I'm thinking, of course, about Meta, and its
smart glasses being banned in some public spaces
and
generally disparaged with names like 'pervert glasses'
. Smart glasses have obviously garnered a real stigma thanks to people drilling out the LED recording light and using them to discreetly record inappropriately and without consent for clout, content, or their own personal use.
This has created a general feeling of malaise around wearables equipped with discreet cameras and microphones in general. Like Meta Glasses, the Live Rewind and Siri Recaps features have accessibility potential for those hard of hearing, but they're going to make most people uncomfortable.
Watch: Audio Intelligence features being announced
@techradar
♬ original sound - TechRadar
Apple is keen to evidence its trustworthiness, with on-device AI and Private Cloud Compute and an insistence that it doesn't record or log audio and transcripts. However, if people think they're being discreetly recorded without their permission, it's possible Apple Watch wearers could experience their own slice of the abuse hurled at Meta Glasses wearers.
What to read next

I wrote earlier this year that
wearable tech has to separate itself from surveillance capitalism if it wishes to be cool again
. It seems Apple has taken a step in the other direction.
Update: Apple has published an article on its website, specifically about Audio Intelligence
, and much has been made about how Audio Intelligence protects user privacy and is used responsibly. You can
read the full article here
.
In short, Apple says audio is not recorded or stored because "there is no recording to share, forward, or produce if requested by any party, because no recording exists".

data.title: Samsung Debuts zHBM Prototype, Stacking Memory Directly on AI Accelerators
data.author: peter_d_sherman
data.article_summary: 三星在FMS 2026展示zHBM、zNAND-O及400层以上V10 BV-NAND。zHBM将HBM垂直堆叠于AI加速器上，最高性能提升至HBM5的8倍，能效提升3倍；zNAND-O结合V-NAND与TSV，提升容量、带宽和响应速度。此外，三星还展示HBM4E、HBM5及LPDDR5X-PIM等技术。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

Samsung Debuts zHBM Prototype, Stacking Memory Directly on AI Accelerators

스크롤 이동 상태바
Kim Kyung-ryun, Vice President of DRAM Development at Samsung Electronics, introduces zHBM. (Source: Samsung Electronics)
Samsung Electronics unveiled next-generation 3D memory technologies, including z-axis High Bandwidth Memory (zHBM) and zNAND-O, as the company seeks to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing artificial intelligence market.
Samsung on Aug. 5 showcased mockups of zHBM and zNAND-O for the first time at the Future of Memory and Storage (FMS) 2026 conference in California. During a keynote presentation on Aug. 4 local time, the company also outlined its vision for maximizing performance and power efficiency in high-performance computing (HPC) and AI systems through the use of zHBM, zNAND-O and other advanced memory technologies.
zHBM Delivers Up to Eight Times Higher Performance Through New Architecture
zHBM mockup. (Source: Samsung Electronics)
zHBM is a next-generation architecture that vertically stacks HBM on top of AI accelerators, or xPUs, along the z-axis. The design minimizes the distance data must travel between memory and AI processors, improving bandwidth and power efficiency while supporting the ultra-high-speed data processing required for training and inference of large-scale AI models.
Conventional architectures place HBM around the AI accelerator. Samsung said that approach faces limitations in meeting the performance requirements of next-generation HPC and AI infrastructure.
According to the company, zHBM can deliver up to eight times the data-processing performance of eighth-generation High Bandwidth Memory (HBM5) while improving performance per watt by a factor of three. Thermal resistance is reduced by more than half, enhancing both system stability and energy efficiency.
Samsung described zHBM as a customizable family of 3D memory products. The architecture allows customers to add semiconductor intellectual property (IP) blocks to an interlayer positioned between the memory and AI accelerator. These blocks can be tailored to expand memory capacity or optimize accelerator performance for specific workloads.
The company said it plans to work closely with customers to co-optimize AI processors and memory systems and maximize the performance potential of zHBM.
Samsung Reveals HBM-Like zNAND-O and 400-Plus-Layer V10 BV-NAND
zNAND-O mockup. (Source: Samsung Electronics)
Samsung also introduced zNAND-O, a next-generation high-performance NAND flash family currently under development. The technology combines Samsung's vertical V-NAND stacking architecture with Through-Silicon Via (TSV) technology. TSVs are used in HBM to electrically and physically connect vertically stacked DRAM dies. Samsung's zNAND-O adopts a structure similar to High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), which is being developed by SK Hynix and Sandisk.
The "O" in zNAND-O refers to on-device AI applications. Samsung demonstrated four-layer and eight-layer 3D-packaged V-NAND configurations designed to deliver high space efficiency, increased read bandwidth and faster response times. The company said the technology is well suited for environments requiring real-time processing of large volumes of data.
During the keynote, Samsung also unveiled its V10 Bonding Vertical (BV)-NAND technology featuring more than 400 layers. The next-generation NAND architecture improves both performance and power efficiency. The displayed zNAND-O mockup was built using the V10 NAND platform.
BV-NAND separates the NAND cell array and peripheral circuitry onto different wafers before vertically bonding them together. The process utilizes advanced wafer-bonding technology that enables three-dimensional integration of multiple wafers.
Samsung further combines the approach with a three-stack architecture, in which V-NAND cells are manufactured in three separate stacks and then vertically interconnected. The company said memory density improves by approximately 58% compared with the previous V9 generation, enabling greater storage capacity within the same footprint. Read, write and input/output performance have also been enhanced.
HBM4E, HBM5 and Processing-in-Memory Technologies Also Displayed
Samsung Electronics' exhibition booth at FMS 2026. (Source: Samsung Electronics)
Samsung's exhibition area featured more than 30 memory products spanning DRAM and NAND technologies. Highlights included a next-generation AI computing platform based on HBM4E, wafer samples, and an HBM5 mockup incorporating Heat Path Block (HPB) technology. HPB adds vertical heat-dissipation channels along the sides of HBM core dies to improve thermal management.
The company also showcased LPDDR5X-PIM, which combines low-power LPDDR5X DRAM with Processing-in-Memory (PIM) functionality. Samsung described the product as the world's first implementation of its kind, enabling more efficient data movement a

data.title: More questions about whether researchers can trust OpenAI with unpublished math
data.author: pred_
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI是否利用研究者与模型的未公开交流，生成并发布相近数学成果却未署名，以及这暴露出的数据治理与学术伦理问题。

不同观点：
• **涉嫌挪用、应归功于研究者**：nezi、angry_octet认为，研究者提供思路后被“抢先发表”，若发生在人类合作者之间显然不道德；OpenAI至少应提供署名、补偿或免费算力支持。模型作为中介，可能在传递信息时抹去来源，导致他人“无意中抢先”。
• **模型可能独立发现**：sashank_1509认为，预训练中的聊天数据即使提升直觉，模型在可验证数学上的强化学习和大规模搜索也可能独立发展出相关技巧；OpenAI或许即使没有这些对话也能解决问题。
• **证据不足、质疑指控**：sk4rekr0w、Legend2440认为目前只是“有人曾与AI讨论过该主题”，且当事人未声称已有完整证明，不能据此认定抄袭。bamb008还指出，相关数学家此前介绍该构造时未明确说明关键论证源自自己。
• **对数据安全的系统性担忧**：多位评论者认为企业有强烈动机留存和利用用户数据，模型的记忆能力使私人对话被转化为竞争成果的风险高于传统云服务；用户很难真正确认数据未被训练或内部使用。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“模型独立发现”与“受未公开对话影响”如何区分、能否验证，以及成果归属和责任如何界定。有人建议用“诱饵短语”等实验测试记忆与泄露；另有评论怀疑OpenAI在得知相关数据可能存在后仍大规模生成输出，像是有意规避来源。

data.title: Cognition launches new SWE-2 model, Rivaling Fable 5.1 and GPT-Astra
data.author: seelos
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了最新编程模型SWE-2：基于2.8万亿参数的Kimi K3，通过强化学习提升代码能力与成本效率。在FrontierCode 1.1 Main上得分50%，性能接近顶尖模型但价格低64%。SWE-2探索更聚焦、减少冗余操作，代码测试和验证能力更强。其训练采用多档推理强度、成本惩罚、奖励基线优化、高效推理服务及更丰富的数据环境，目前已在Devin多平台上线。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Cognition/Devin 发布的 SWE-2 模型，评论集中于基准成绩可信度、模型来源、实际使用体验及开放性。

不同观点：
• **质疑基准泛化能力**：SWE-2 在 Terminal Bench 2.1 达到92.8%，但在较新的 Terminal Bench 4 仅27.3%，被认为可能存在“benchmaxxing”（针对旧测试集优化），且官方为何不展示更多指标受到质疑。  
• **质疑模型创新与公司信誉**：SWE-2 据称基于 Kimi K3 后训练，并非全新模型；有人联想到 Cognition 过去演示中“自主完成任务”却实际跑偏的案例，认为性能提升应谨慎解读。也有人认为基于优秀底模进行强化本身仍有价值。  
• **关注开放权重与竞争格局**：评论者希望模型开放权重，并质疑若是闭源，为什么不选择更便宜、更快的 DeepSeek Flash 4.1；认为开发者不想继续依赖少数闭源大厂。  
• **实际体验偏负面但期待改进**：有人称 Devin/SWE 产品“持续难用”，也有人反馈 SWE 1.6 适合小任务、1.7 却低效且反复，期待 SWE-2 改善；少数用户认可 Cognition 的工程能力。  
• **适用场景存在分歧**：专注软件工程的模型未必适合模拟软件等跨学科工作，后者需要物理、数学与编程的综合理解。  
• **效率与成本争议**：有人认为成绩提升主要来自大幅减少输出 token，官方只展示成本、不展示耗时和 token 数，可能掩盖关键变化；也有人注意到其任务成本或许仍高于单 token 更便宜的模型。

补充讨论：有评论猜测 SWE-2 可能参与了 RSA-260 因式分解相关工作，但未形成明确结论；另有人质疑发帖账号过新及文章有“标题党”嫌疑。

training infrastructure and recipe. The key addition is an RL algorithm that trains all reasoning-effort levels in a single run, advancing the whole cost–performance frontier.

The result is our closest model yet to the frontier. On FrontierCode 1.1 Main and DeepSWE 1.1, SWE-2 beats SWE-1.7 and Grok 4.6 on both score and cost, matches GPT-5.6 Sol and Fable 5/5.1 at a fraction of their price, and comes within a few points of GPT-6 Astra at a quarter of the cost.

, a 2.8T-parameter model that had already undergone extensive RL for agentic coding. As with SWE-1.7, our RL still finds substantial headroom, adding 5–6 points on many benchmarks and shifting K3’s entire cost–performance frontier.

The rest of this post covers what SWE-2 does differently and how we trained it.
We begin with SWE-2’s behavior, focusing on the characteristics that make it more efficient and intelligent compared to our previous models. Then, we detail the post-training advances behind SWE-2:
Cost penalties.
We apply a linear cost penalty per effort level in a single RL run, with each penalty tuned to the local slope of the base model’s Pareto frontier. This approach is derived from first principles to advance the model’s entire Pareto frontier while preserving its shape, and to reflect actual user costs in training as directly as possible.
Reward baselines.
We derive the length-weighted reward baseline we have used since SWE-1.6 and show how it significantly stabilizes training.
RL rollout serving.
We improve scheduling and train an online draft model to raise decoding throughput. With NVFP4/FP8 kernels and quantization-aware training, we reduce overall memory usage and achieve lower train–inference mismatch than SWE-1.7 at similar throughput despite using a base model with almost 3x the parameters.
Training data.
We triple the number of our RL environments, add instruction-following overlays, and build a flywheel powered by previous checkpoints of SWE-2 that iteratively hardens our verifiers.
SWE-2 is available starting today in Devin

. We’re also rolling it out on

and

.

#
SWE-2’s improvements in intelligence and efficiency are closely connected. Stronger engineering judgment allows the agent to write more complete solutions alongside fewer detours and redundant reads. On FrontierCode 1.1 Main, we see that SWE-2 medium scores higher than SWE-1.7 while taking 58% fewer turns and costing 81% less on average.

While boosting performance, this led to user feedback that SWE-1.7 tended to over-explore and overthink on simple tasks. Promisingly on this front, we find that the largest efficiency gains from SWE-2 come from

: higher intelligence allows the model to judge which parts of the codebase actually matter for a task. This allows SWE-2 to begin implementation sooner: on FrontierCode 1.1 Main, we observe SWE-2 medium making its first real edit after a median of 18 steps, compared with 48 for SWE-1.7.

SWE-2 is better at writing tests that check an implementation end-to-end, catching regressions and edge cases more reliably.

When the obvious path is blocked, SWE-2 is more willing to look for another route to the same answer. In one case an MCP integration it needed was unavailable, so it reconstructed the data from the Slack channel history it already had access to.

data.title: The Deathray: A simple way for an untrusted site to freeze a Mac
data.author: auberonedu
data.article_summary: 文章介绍“Deathray”漏洞：不可信网站可通过WebGPU提交包含无限循环的着色器，耗尽Mac GPU资源，导致WindowServer失去响应、桌面卡死，最终触发看门狗重启。该问题在M系列Mac的Chrome、Firefox和Safari上均可复现，其他系统通常仅影响标签页。作者认为WebGPU缺乏有效的着色器抢占机制，并已向苹果报告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：浏览器中的 WebGPU/图形计算死循环可能拖垮 GPU，进而导致窗口系统、浏览器或整个操作系统卡死，讨论集中于其影响范围、安全性及是否应限制 WebGPU。

不同观点：
• **严重性与安全风险**：sgentle认为“让电脑崩溃”可被用于强迫用户点击授权、关闭广告拦截器或观看广告，属于可被滥用的拒绝服务（DoS）问题；achierius则指出它通常不能直接窃取秘密或劫持身份，因此未必达到传统安全漏洞标准，但仍然相当恶劣，应尽快修复。  
• **浏览器暴露硬件接口的担忧**：xoa对浏览器逐渐成为“操作系统之上的操作系统”持谨慎态度，已在 Firefox 中禁用 WebGPU、WebGL，并质疑为何默认屏蔽 easyeda.com；ilnmtlbnm则担心类似问题会促使厂商彻底禁用 WebGPU。  
• **实际影响因平台而异**：Windows 11 用户称 Teams 会随机黑屏；多位 Mac 用户报告 GPU 负载后 WindowServer 或整个系统严重变慢，甚至需重启。也有人表示 iOS 27 完全不受影响。  
• **技术机制讨论**：krackers询问 GPU 为何不能像 CPU 一样由内核调度、避免死循环独占资源；StilesCrisis补充 Metal shader 中的 Duff’s Device 可触发编译器严重故障，但未造成内核恐慌。  
• **类似攻击与趣味案例**：评论提到无限 JavaScript、Three.js 加载超大模型、旧版 iOS 特殊 Unicode 字符等也能制造假死或崩溃；有人担心尝试点击演示链接，也有人询问这是否解释了网页游戏 Oregon Trail Deluxe 的冻结。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“仅造成拒绝服务是否足以构成安全漏洞”，以及应修复隔离机制还是限制 WebGPU 功能。
